title: Metal Assays and Their Saboteurs: Calcium, Ferrozine Iron, ALP and GGT
summary: Learn how free and total calcium, ferrozine iron and zinc-dependent ALP are measured, how chelators such as EDTA and gadolinium contrast distort them in the tube, why TIBC methods disagree, and why a drug-raised GGT is a real enzyme induction.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 28 Hits 11 (iron/TIBC ferrozine chemistry), 12 (GGT as the induced enzyme; ALP inhibition by chelators) and 14 (calcium: free vs protein-bound; ISE; chelation). Checked against Lian 2018, Desgagnés 2025, Lima-Oliveira 2014, Lippi 2014, Millán 2016, Hirayama 2017, Serhan 2020, Mahant 2023, Guo 2022, Hadzagic-Catibusic 2017 and Koenig 2015, all read as Europe PMC full text. Qualified: GGT induction by drugs and alcohol is a real rise, not a false result; TIBC is method-dependent (calculated, indirect, direct; not harmonised); acidified-serum ISE for total calcium could not be verified. Not verified, so not taught: the ALP (p-nitrophenylphosphate) and GGT (carboxy-nitroanilide) substrates and 410 nm reads, ALP inhibition by citrate, oxalate and fluoride, the reviewer’s TIBC procedure (excess ferric chloride, pH shift, falling colour), the 562 nm read and magenta colour (the source read gives 563 nm), the Siemens Advia 571 nm read, Arsenazo III at 650 nm in imidazole pH 6.0, citrate interference with Arsenazo III, and acidified-serum ISE total calcium.

objectives: Describe how free and total calcium, ferrozine iron and ALP are measured, and why calcium binding and ALP metal cofactors matter.
Recognise the pattern of EDTA carry-over and the method-dependent effects of gadolinium contrast on calcium and TIBC.
Distinguish analytical interference by chelators from a real GGT rise caused by enzyme induction, and explain why TIBC results vary by method.

scenes.title: Three odd results
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three results land on one bench. (1) A well outpatient’s serum: calcium and magnesium very low, potassium high, ALP low. (2) A patient on carbamazepine: GGT high, every other liver test normal. (3) A TIBC drawn shortly after a gadolinium-enhanced MRI reads higher than expected. Question token: “Patient, tube, or method?”

cues.text: Invented case: a well outpatient’s serum shows very low calcium and magnesium, high potassium, and a low alkaline phosphatase.
A patient taking carbamazepine has a high GGT with every other liver test normal. And a TIBC drawn soon after a gadolinium MRI reads high.
For each one: is the patient changing, the tube, or the method?

scenes.title: How the metal assays work
scenes.altText: Three method cards. Calcium: about half of plasma calcium is free (ionized) and the rest is protein-bound, mostly to albumin, with a few per cent complexed with anions such as citrate and lactate; free calcium is measured by an ion-selective electrode on an anaerobic sample (one large study standardised it to pH 7.40), while total calcium is commonly measured by colorimetric dyes such as o-cresolphthalein or arsenazo. Iron: an acid reagent strips Fe³⁺ from transferrin, a reductant converts it to Fe²⁺, and ferrozine binds Fe²⁺ 3:1 to form an intensely coloured complex absorbing at about 563 nm. ALP: the enzyme needs two zinc ions and one magnesium ion at its active site.

cues.text: Calcium first. About half of plasma calcium is free, or ionized, and only that half is biologically active. The rest is bound to proteins, mostly albumin, with a few percent held by anions such as citrate and lactate.
Ionized calcium is measured by an ion-selective electrode on an anaerobic sample. Total calcium is commonly measured with a colour dye such as o-cresolphthalein or arsenazo.

Iron next. An acid reagent strips ferric iron from transferrin, a reductant turns it into ferrous iron, and ferrozine wraps three molecules around each ferrous ion, giving an intense colour read at about five hundred and sixty-three nanometres.
Alkaline phosphatase is a metalloenzyme. Its active site holds two zinc ions and one magnesium ion, and it needs them to work.

props.title: ALP = metalloenzyme
lines: 2 Zn²⁺ + 1 Mg²⁺ at the active site

scenes.title: Chelators in the tube
scenes.altText: EDTA card: EDTA works as an anticoagulant by chelating divalent ions (calcium, magnesium, zinc, manganese). In an experiment adding K2EDTA blood to lithium-heparin blood, calcium, magnesium, iron, chloride and LD fell and potassium rose significantly from 5% contamination; ALT, bilirubin, creatinine and lipase were unchanged up to 43%. An earlier survey of EDTA-contaminated samples (cited in the same paper) found ALP about −70% and UIBC about +335%. Gadolinium card: gadolinium MRI contrast agents are strong chelators; with some agents (gadodiamide, gadoversetamide) o-cresolphthalein calcium read falsely low, some arsenazo reagents read high, and ferrozine TIBC read high; in one study an ISE and two arsenazo assays were unaffected.

cues.text: Now add a chelator to the tube. EDTA prevents clotting by grabbing divalent ions: calcium, magnesium, zinc and manganese. Carry-over of EDTA into a serum or heparin tube takes those ions out of the measurement.
In one experiment, just five percent K2 EDTA contamination significantly lowered calcium, magnesium and iron and raised potassium. ALT, bilirubin, creatinine and lipase did not change.
Alkaline phosphatase loses its zinc and magnesium too: a survey of contaminated samples found ALP about seventy percent low.

Gadolinium contrast agents are chelators as well. With some agents, o-cresolphthalein calcium reads falsely low, some arsenazo reagents read high, and ferrozine TIBC reads high. The direction depends on the agent and the method.

scenes.title: Inducers and TIBC methods
scenes.altText: GGT card: GGT activity is inducible by drugs; carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital and others can raise it, carbamazepine-related rises are attributed to enzyme induction without liver injury, and GGT is a traditional marker of alcohol consumption — the increase is real (biological), not an analytical artefact. TIBC card: TIBC can be calculated (serum iron + UIBC), measured indirectly (saturation then precipitation) or measured directly; methods are not harmonised, and in one study direct TIBC averaged about 34–36 µg/dL higher. Ferrozine UIBC can read falsely low or zero in some sera. Hook answers: (1) suspect EDTA contamination and redraw; (2) enzyme induction is likely, interpret with the clinical picture; (3) gadolinium can falsely raise ferrozine TIBC, so note the timing and method.

cues.text: Not every surprise is an artefact. GGT is an inducible enzyme: carbamazepine can raise it without liver injury, phenytoin and phenobarbital raise it too, and it is a classic marker of alcohol use. That increase is real, made by the patient, not by the assay.

TIBC has more than one method. It can be calculated as serum iron plus UIBC, measured indirectly by saturating and precipitating, or measured directly, and the methods are not harmonised. In one study, direct TIBC averaged about thirty-five micrograms per decilitre higher.
Back to the hook. The well outpatient with low calcium, low magnesium, high potassium and low ALP fits EDTA carry-over: redraw before treating.
The isolated high GGT on carbamazepine fits enzyme induction. And the TIBC after gadolinium may be falsely high, so note the timing and the method.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Albumin-adjusted calcium beats total calcium” (✓ in two large studies, adjustment formulas did no better than unadjusted total calcium; if in doubt, measure ionized calcium); “Low Ca, low Mg, high K and low ALP in a well patient means a disease” (✓ suspect EDTA contamination and redraw); “Drug-raised GGT is a false result” (✓ enzyme induction is a real increase in enzyme activity).

cues.text: Trap one: albumin-adjusted calcium is always better than total calcium. No: in two large studies, adjustment formulas did no better than the unadjusted total. If in doubt, measure ionized calcium.
Trap two: low calcium, low magnesium, high potassium and low ALP in a well patient mean disease. Think EDTA carry-over first, and redraw.
Trap three: a GGT raised by phenytoin is a false result. No: enzyme induction by the drug is a real rise in enzyme activity.

props.title: ✗ “Adjusted calcium is always better.”
lines: ✓ No better than total; measure ionized

scenes.title: Pickpocket and factory
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Chelators are PICKPOCKETS in the tube: EDTA steals calcium, magnesium and the zinc that ALP needs, so those results drop. Inducing drugs run the GGT FACTORY overtime in the patient, so the rise is real.” Tokens: pickpocket = chelator (tube) · factory = inducer (patient). A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: chelators are pickpockets in the tube. EDTA steals calcium, magnesium and the zinc that alkaline phosphatase needs, so those results drop. Inducers run the GGT factory overtime inside the patient, so that rise is real.

Where it breaks: chelators can push some results up, not down, such as ferrozine TIBC with gadolinium, some arsenazo calcium methods, and UIBC with EDTA; and the size of every effect depends on the agent and the method.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Chelators (EDTA, some gadolinium agents) distort metal assays in the tube: calcium, magnesium, iron and ALP often fall”, “Inducers in the patient (enzyme-inducing drugs such as carbamazepine) raise GGT for real”.

cues.text: Chelators such as EDTA and some gadolinium contrast agents distort metal-dependent results in the tube, often lowering calcium, magnesium and alkaline phosphatase, while enzyme-inducing drugs such as carbamazepine raise gamma-glutamyltransferase for real.

props.label: Chelators in the tube: Ca · Mg · iron · ALP often fall
Inducers in the patient: GGT rises for real

explanation.what: Plain language: some tests measure metals, or enzymes that need metals. Chemicals that grab metals (chelators) can steal them in the tube and make results wrong, while some drugs make the body produce more GGT, which is a true rise; alcohol use also raises GGT. Scientific terms: free (ionized) vs protein-bound calcium, ion-selective electrode (ISE), o-cresolphthalein (OCP), arsenazo, ferrozine, Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺, transferrin, UIBC, TIBC (calculated, indirect, direct), metalloenzyme, K2EDTA carry-over, gadolinium contrast agents, enzyme induction.
explanation.why: About half of plasma calcium is bound to proteins (mostly albumin), so total calcium does not always reflect the active free fraction. Colorimetric metal assays and metal-dependent enzymes depend on free metal ions, so chelators in the sample remove or compete for them. Enzyme inducers increase GGT synthesis, so the measured activity truly rises.
explanation.measure: Free calcium: ISE on an anaerobic sample (one study standardised to pH 7.40). Total calcium: colorimetric dyes (OCP, arsenazo). Iron: acid strips Fe³⁺ from transferrin, reductant gives Fe²⁺, ferrozine binds 3:1, coloured complex at about 563 nm. UIBC: multi-step ferrozine method; TIBC calculated as iron + UIBC, or indirect, or direct. EDTA carry-over (5%): calcium, magnesium, iron down, potassium up; ALP about −70% in a survey. Gadolinium (some agents): OCP calcium down, some arsenazo up, ferrozine TIBC up.
explanation.differs: Free vs total calcium; albumin-adjusted vs unadjusted calcium (adjustment did no better in two large studies); analytical interference in the tube (chelators) vs biological change in the patient (induction); calculated vs indirect vs direct TIBC.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: recognising EDTA contamination from low calcium, low magnesium, high potassium and low ALP; which iron form ferrozine binds; why isolated GGT rises on anticonvulsants or alcohol; what fraction of calcium is protein-bound; gadolinium effects on calcium methods.

questions.stem: A well outpatient’s lithium-heparin sample shows very low calcium and magnesium, high potassium and low ALP. The patient has no symptoms. What is the best next step?

options.text: Suspect K2EDTA carry-over and request a correctly collected repeat sample
options.rationale: Correct. EDTA chelates calcium, magnesium and zinc (lowering ALP) and K2EDTA contamination raises potassium; a redraw resolves carry-over.

options.text: Report the results and recommend urgent calcium replacement
options.rationale: Incorrect. The pattern in a well patient suggests an artefact; treating spurious hypocalcaemia can harm the patient.

options.text: Repeat the tests on the same sample after dilution
options.rationale: Incorrect. Dilution does not remove EDTA from the sample; the chelation persists.

options.text: Report hypophosphatasia because ALP is low
options.rationale: Incorrect. A low ALP with low calcium and magnesium and high potassium points to EDTA contamination, not a primary ALP disorder.

questions.stem: In the ferrozine serum iron method, which form of iron forms the coloured complex that is measured?

options.text: Ferrous iron (Fe²⁺), after acid release from transferrin and reduction
options.rationale: Correct. The acid reagent frees Fe³⁺ from transferrin, a reductant gives Fe²⁺, and ferrozine binds Fe²⁺ 3:1 to give a coloured complex absorbing at about 563 nm.

options.text: Ferric iron (Fe³⁺) still bound to transferrin
options.rationale: Incorrect. Iron must be released from transferrin and reduced before ferrozine can bind it.

options.text: Ferritin iron released by an antibody
options.rationale: Incorrect. Ferritin is a storage protein; the serum iron method measures iron stripped from transferrin.
Incorrect. The method measures iron stripped from transferrin, not iron inside hemoglobin.

questions.stem: A patient taking phenytoin has a raised GGT, with ALT, AST, ALP and bilirubin all normal. Which statement best explains the GGT?

options.text: Phenytoin induces GGT, so the measured activity truly rises without liver injury
options.rationale: Correct. GGT activity is inducible by drugs, and phenytoin, phenobarbital and carbamazepine are among those that raise it; the increase is real, not an analytical error.

options.text: Phenytoin interferes with the GGT reagent, so the result is analytically false
options.rationale: Incorrect. The mechanism is enzyme induction in the patient, not interference in the assay.

options.text: The pattern proves extrahepatic biliary obstruction
options.rationale: Incorrect. Nothing in the stem points to obstruction: ALP and bilirubin are normal, and an isolated GGT rise on a known inducer fits induction.

options.text: The sample is contaminated with EDTA
options.rationale: Incorrect. EDTA carry-over lowers metal-dependent results such as calcium and ALP and raises potassium; it would not explain an isolated high GGT with normal ALP.

Acid releases Fe³⁺ from transferrin, reductant gives Fe²⁺, ferrozine binds Fe²⁺ 3:1 with an intense colour absorbing at about 563 nm.

claims.text: ALP needs two Zn²⁺ and one Mg²⁺ at its active site.
EDTA chelates divalent ions; 5% K2EDTA lowers calcium, magnesium, iron and raises potassium; ALP about −70% in a cited survey.
claims.note: The ALP and UIBC figures come from an earlier survey cited by Lima-Oliveira 2014, not from their own experiment.

claims.text: Gadolinium agents: OCP calcium low, some arsenazo high, ferrozine TIBC high; agent- and method-dependent.
TIBC calculated, indirect or direct; not harmonised; direct averaged ~34–36 µg/dL higher in one study; ferrozine UIBC can read falsely low.

GGT activity is inducible by drugs; carbamazepine, phenytoin and phenobarbital can raise it; carbamazepine rises attributed to induction without liver injury; GGT is a traditional marker of alcohol consumption.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 28 Hit 12 says phenytoin, phenobarbital and heavy alcohol “falsely elevate” GGT. Hadzagic-Catibusic 2017 and Koenig 2015 describe GGT as an inducible enzyme whose activity truly rises with these exposures; the lesson teaches induction as a real (biological) rise, not an analytical false result (register flag rv-ch28-ggt-induction-real).

Ch. 28 Hit 11 presents one TIBC chemistry as the method. Mahant 2023 shows TIBC is calculated (iron + UIBC), measured indirectly or directly, with non-harmonised results (direct about 34–36 µg/dL higher), and Guo 2022 reports unreliable low ferrozine UIBC readings in some sera; the reviewer’s ferric-chloride/pH-shift procedure was not verified (register flag rv-ch28-tibc-method).

Ch. 28 Hit 14 says acidified serum on a calcium ISE gives total calcium and unacidified gives ionized calcium. No open source read in this session described acidified-serum ISE total calcium; Lian 2018 measured total calcium colorimetrically and free calcium by ISE on anaerobic samples, and Lippi 2014 shows colorimetric total calcium is biased by some gadolinium agents (register flag rv-ch28-calcium-acidified-ise).
